options.text: Charles Bonnet syndrome, A 87-year-old lady with a history of falls was brought to the A&E by the paramedics. She is agitated

correct_answer.text: Charles Bonnet syndrome, A 87-year-old lady with a history of falls was brought to the A&E by the paramedics. She is agitated

questions.explanation:
Case 1 is Diogenes syndrome (or 'senile squalor syndrome') refers to severe self-neglect seen in somewhat eccentric and reclusive elderly
individuals. They become increasingly isolated and neglect themselves, living in �lthy, poor conditions. It can be viewed as the response of
someone with a particular personality type to the hardships of old age and loneliness (Howard & Bergman 1993). They are often oblivious to
their condition and resistant to help, making management notoriously di�cult as it is very hard to form a therapeutic alliance.  
Case 2 is late onset paraphrenia. Persecutory delusions are the most common symptoms of late paraphrenia; they are found in around 90%
of patients. Auditory hallucinations occur in approximately 75% of cases. Visual hallucinations are observed in up to 60% of patients. Few
patients may present with delusions only (10-20%). Partition delusions (attack through the wall, neighbours spying via any 'partition') are
common. According to ICD-10,  patients must either be diagnosed as having delusional disorder or schizophrenia - no separate diagnosis
exists for paraphrenia.  

Case 3 is a typical presentation of Charles Bonnet syndrome. 
Case 4 is delirium. The salient features include rapid onset of clinical features with �uctuations in severity over minutes and hours (even
back to apparent normality), clouding of consciousness with reduced attention span and distractibility, global impairment of cognition with
disorientation, and impairment of recent memory and abstract thinking.

options.text: Cortical atrophy in parietal and temporal lobes
Reduction in oxygen and glucose metabolism in temporal and posterior parietal lobes

correct_answer.text: Cortical atrophy in parietal and temporal lobes

questions.explanation:
CT scan shows cortical atrophy especially over parietal and temporal lobes, and dilatation of the third ventricle, which correlates with
cognitive impairment (most common picture). In the advanced stage of the disease, the frontal lobe is a�ected.  
SPECT measures cerebral blood �ow and in Alzheimer's disease, there is a characteristic reduction in blood �ow in temporal and parietal
regions. SPECT could distinguish speci�c features of dementia of Alzheimer type at early stages and frontal lobe dementia.  
PET scan measures oxygen and glucose metabolism directly. In Alzheimer's disease, there is 20-30% reduction in oxygen and glucose
metabolism in temporal and posterior parietal lobes.  
In Magnetic resonance spectroscopy, there is an abnormal synthesis of membrane phospholipids early in the disease and reduced levels of
N-Acetyl aspartate.

questions.explanation:
Case 1 is Binswanger's disease (progressive small vessel disease). It is subcortical dementia with a clinical course characterised by slow
intellectual decline and generalised slowing. MRI scan shows small distinct infarcts (lacunae) or more widespread white matter changes
(leukoariasis).  
Case 2 is new variant CJD. The rise of vCJD followed an epidemic of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) in cattle. The disease in humans
a�ects mainly young men in their 20s and is characterised by early anxiety and depressive symptoms, followed by personality changes, and
�nally progressive dementia. Ataxia and myoclonus are prominent and the typical course is 1-2 yrs until death.  
Case 3 is Normal pressure hydrocephalus. NPH is a syndrome where there is dilatation of cerebral ventricles, especially the third ventricle)
and normal CSF pressure at lumbar puncture. It typically presents with the triad of dementia, gait ataxia, and urinary incontinence.  

Case 4 is General Paresis of insane (GPI). It is an impairment of mental function caused by damage to the brain from untreated syphilis. This
damage can produce hallucinations and delusions (grandiosity). Brief, sharp "lightning" pains occur with tabes dorsalis. Eye changes
including abnormal pupil response, mood changes (euphoria and mania), overactive re�exes, personality changes and speech changes are
also noted. General paresis usually begins about 15 - 20 years after the syphilis infection. Cerebral atrophy and gliosis, dominantly in the
frontal lobes are well-known neuropathological �ndings of GPI.
